reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Anterior Shoulder Dislocation Bankart Lesion: squared-off shoulder contour and severe pain after fall onto outstretched arm. 22M college wrestler presenting with right arm held abducted and externally rotated, loss of deltoid roundness, and subglenoid humeral head on AP X-ray.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Anterior Shoulder Dislocation Bankart Lesion.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Anterior Shoulder Dislocation Bankart Lesion.
reference_soap.plan: Treat this as an urgent shoulder dislocation: document distal pulses, capillary refill, motor function, and axillary-nerve sensation before and after reduction; obtain appropriate pre- and post-reduction radiographs; provide analgesia/sedation and perform reduction only in a monitored setting by trained clinicians. Immobilize after successful reduction and arrange orthopedic follow-up for recurrent-instability risk. Escalate immediately for an absent pulse, worsening numbness/weakness, or suspected fracture.

teaching.diagnosis: Anterior shoulder dislocation with Bankart lesion
teaching.one_liner: 22M wrestler with a squared-off shoulder contour and severe pain after a fall onto an outstretched arm.
red_flags: Neurovascular compromise (axillary nerve) must be checked before and after reduction

must_ask.say: Can you describe exactly how you fell and what position your arm was in?

must_ask.objective: Assess the shoulder contour and position
must_ask.say: Does your shoulder look different, like squared off compared to the other side?

must_ask.objective: Screen for numbness over the shoulder (axillary nerve)
must_ask.say: Do you have any numbness over the outer part of your shoulder?
Has your shoulder ever popped out before?

must_ask.objective: Explain the reduction and post-reduction care
must_ask.say: Because this appears dislocated, trained clinicians need to reduce it urgently after checking blood flow and nerve function; those checks are repeated afterward, followed by a sling and follow-up.

history.answer: I fell hard onto my right arm during wrestling practice an hour ago, and my shoulder is in unbearable pain and looks completely out of place.
The pain is only in my right shoulder; my left shoulder, elbows, and all other joints feel completely normal.
It started suddenly about an hour ago right after I hit the mat during my match.
It is a severe, tearing, deep pain that I would rate as a 9 out of 10.
The shoulder looks flattened and squared-off on the side rather than rounded, but there is no warmth or red discoloration.
No, I have never had any morning stiffness in my joints.
Any attempt to move or touch the shoulder causes agonizing pain, so holding my arm completely still with my other hand is the only way to tolerate it.
I cannot use my right arm to reach or lift anything, but I can still move my fingers and wrist.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or sweats.
An opponent took me down and I landed heavily on my outstretched right hand with my arm twisted out to the side, and I felt a sudden pop in the shoulder.
No, I have never dislocated this shoulder or had any shoulder trouble before today.
No, I have not experienced any fatigue, low-grade fevers, or unintentional weight loss.
No, I do not have any facial rashes, psoriasis patches, mouth sores, hair loss, or red, irritated eyes.
No, I have never had lower back stiffness in the mornings, heel pain, or swollen fingers or toes.
No, I have not had any diarrhea, burning with urination, discharge, or recent sore throats.
I eat a regular athletic diet, rarely drink alcohol, and have never taken water pills or gout medications.
I have never had any joint injections, joint surgeries, artificial joints, or steroid treatments.
I have been in a monogamous relationship with my girlfriend for two years, and neither of us has any other partners.
The outside curve of my shoulder is flattened and squared off, and I have to hold my arm away from my body because bringing it in hurts too much.
I have some dull numbness over the outside of my upper arm, right over the shoulder muscle patch.
I think my shoulder popped completely out of its socket when I hit the mat.
I'm terrified that I'll need surgery and miss out on the rest of my wrestling season.
I just want you to pop it back into place and give me something strong for the pain.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions or health problems.
I have never had any surgeries or prior hospitalizations.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or supplements.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any nicotine products.
I only have a beer occasionally on social occasions, maybe once every few weeks.
I am a twenty-two-year-old college student and compete on the university wrestling team.
There is no family history of joint diseases, arthritis, or recurrent joint dislocations.

exam.finding: Patient is in acute distress, cradling the right arm supported in slight abduction and external rotation, with a visible loss of the normal rounded contour of the right deltoid and a prominent acromion.
Blood pressure 128/82 mmHg, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, temperature 36.8 degrees Celsius, oxygen saturation 99 percent on room air.

Palpation reveals a distinct hollow beneath the lateral acromion, an anteriorly displaced humeral head palpable in the subcoracoid region, exquisite tenderness over the anterior glenohumeral joint, and active and passive motion are blocked by severe pain.
Right radial and brachial pulses are 2+ and symmetric to the left side, with immediate capillary refill under two seconds in all digits.
Decreased sensation to light touch and pinprick over the lateral aspect of the right upper deltoid badge area, with intact sensation in the median, radial, and ulnar distributions.
Full 5/5 motor strength in right wrist extension, wrist flexion, finger abduction, and thumb opposition, while active deltoid abduction cannot be tested due to severe shoulder pain.
No erythematous rash, psoriatic plaques, tophi, or nail pitting on skin examination.
Normal upright stance and steady, non-antalgic gait without balance disturbance.
